source.title: An Expert Guide To Pattern Mixing
source.author: FashionBeans

tips.text: When mixing patterns, keep to a tight colour palette and add any pop of colour through an accessory or a small detail.
tips.why: Shared colours stop the patterns fighting each other.

tips.text: Pair a large pattern with a small one rather than two patterns of similar size.
tips.why: Contrast in scale keeps the outfit from looking like a picnic blanket.

tips.text: When combining different pattern types, choose ones that look clearly different, such as stripes with florals, not dots with puppytooth.
tips.why: Patterns that are too alike blur together and look like a mistake.

tips.text: If wearing three patterns, make one small, one medium and one large; a patterned tie or pocket square can be the third.
tips.why: Graduated scales let each pattern read on its own.

tips.text: Put the boldest pattern on the outer layer and keep quieter patterns underneath.
tips.why: The loud piece leads and the rest supports it.
Checks are the easiest pattern for most men to wear.

tips.text: When clashing two checks, keep them in a family of related colours.
tips.why: A shared palette lets different-sized checks look deliberate.

tips.text: To mix stripes with stripes, vary their width or direction, for example horizontal stripes under vertical ones.
tips.why: A change of width or direction separates the two layers.

tips.text: For smart stripe-on-stripe outfits, use shades of one colour, such as tonal navy, rather than stark black and white.
tips.why: Tonal stripes look refined; black and white stripes look costume-like.

tips.text: Pair houndstooth only with simple patterns such as a narrow pinstripe or large polka dots.
tips.why: Houndstooth is already busy and fights other complex prints.

tips.text: Tame a paisley piece by repeating one of its colours elsewhere in the outfit.
tips.why: The repeated colour ties an intense print to the rest of the look.

tips.text: Wear polka dots mainly on accessories such as ties, pocket squares and socks, set against straight-line patterns like stripes or checks.
tips.why: Dots are easiest in small doses and contrast well with lines.

tips.text: With a check suit, try a striped tie and a polka-dot pocket square in a sober palette.
tips.why: Three different pattern types in quiet colours mix without clashing.

tips.text: For a casual pattern mix, wear an open check overshirt over a striped knit or a graphic tee.
tips.why: The outer check and inner pattern contrast in type and scale.
